newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil basket rises on gasoline rally.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil basket rises on gasoline rally.

text.p: Venezuela's oil export basket price edged up 13 cents during the week to close Friday at $16.23 per barrel, the Energy and Mines Ministry said in a statement.
Oil traders in the futures markets of New York and London said refinery problems in the United States and Venezuela were to blame for the rising world prices.
Prices fell for three months from a multi-year high in January this year, but have stabilised since March and even showed a modest recovery since June.
The average basket price in August so far was $16.23, against a July average of $15.80 and June at $15.30 per barrel, the Ministry said.

Exxon's U.S. Baytown and Venezuela's Cardon and Curacao refineries all ran into problems with their gasoline producing units in recent weeks, forcing buyers to pay more for their supplies into the huge U.S. market.

Venezuela's basket has averaged $16.57 per barrel so far in 1997, down two cents on last Friday. This was well below 1996's $18.39 average, but still above the government's budgeted $14.00 per barrel.
For 1998, the government budgeted for an average $15.50 per barrel basket.
